paragraphs: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, and Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi, in Rav’s name (I did not find it). (In the Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter Keitzad Mevarkhin, in Rabbi Elazar’s name; in Tanchuma, Re'eh, Rabbi Iva bar Kahana—perhaps they are one.) Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said, “Once,” etc.; Rabbi said, etc.; Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in Rabbi Chanina’s name, etc.; Rabbi Zeira said to him, etc.; three things (Shabbat 121b–122a; see below, Abba bar Ila'ah). “His God instructs him in judgment, teaches him”—Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: so in Yalkut, Isaiah 28, and so it appears in Rashi, Chelek 105a. The Gemara and Ein Yaakov read “Rabbah bar bar Chana said”; this is a scribal error, uncorrected in the new Talmud editions. Rabbi Avin, his father, in his name; in Rabbi Elazar’s name; and Rabbi Assi; Rabbah, end of the proem to Eikhah; in Rabbi Boddai’s name; Rabbi Berekhiah in his name; Gamliel Zuga asked him; and Rabbi Gamliel bar Anina; Rabbi Ze'ira in Rabbi Yehudah’s name; he said in Rabbi Chanina’s name, Shabbat 121b; and Rav Chisda; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Yair in Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair’s name; he said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name (chapter Kol Kitvei); to Rabbi Yirmeyah; He heard Levi expound and kissed him; in Rabbi Mattanah’s name; in Ulla’s name; Rabbah, the proem to Eikhah there; in R. Azariah of Kefar Chattaya’s name; and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Narshiah in Resh Lakish’s name; in R. Shmuel’s name (Yalkut, II Samuel, remez 162); and Rabbi Tanchuma.
